title: MileageTracker
summary: An Android mileage-tracking app with trip capture, classification, vehicle records, and reporting, supported by automated checks and explicit beta release gates.
problem: Drivers need a dependable way to record trip details, organize mileage, and review information for their own records without losing sight of incomplete or unverified entries.
role: Solo developer building the Android application and maintaining its verification and closed-beta checklist.
stakeholders: Drivers recording personal or business mileage
currentStatus: A closed-beta solo foundation. Known blockers, device checks, and release gates remain tracked; no full release is claimed.
publicationBoundary: The five supplied screen recordings are approved for public display, including real trip, profile, and vehicle information. This project description is not tax advice and does not promise CRA acceptance.
limitations: The project remains a closed-beta foundation with release gates still tracked.
No tax advice or CRA-acceptance promise is made.
The public screen recordings show owner-approved real trip, profile, and vehicle information; they do not change the project's closed-beta status.
claimPolicy: Do not describe the project as fully released or generally available.
Do not promise CRA acceptance or present the app as tax advice.
The owner approved the five supplied recordings, including the visible account email, trip records, and vehicle details, for public display.
evidence: Automated unit and Android UI coverage spans validation, interrupted-trip recovery, synchronization, authentication, exports, and core screens.
A closed-beta checklist separates implemented features, known blockers, device smoke tests, emulator-rule checks, and release gates.
The public GitHub repository is available for code review.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: MileageTracker is an Android app for recording and organizing vehicle mileage. Its project scope includes trip capture, business or personal classification, vehicle records, and reporting.

sections.heading: Role and implementation
paragraphs: I am building the app as a solo developer using Kotlin and Jetpack Compose, with Room, Hilt, and Firebase in the implementation stack.
bullets: Trip capture and durable GPS capture.
Business or personal classification and vehicle management.
Odometer, expense, receipt, and report workflows.

sections.heading: Verification and release gates
paragraphs: Automated unit and Android UI tests cover validation, interrupted-trip recovery, synchronization, authentication, exports, and core screens. The closed-beta checklist keeps implemented behavior separate from known blockers, device smoke tests, emulator-rule checks, and release gates.

sections.heading: Evidence and limits
paragraphs: The owner approved all five supplied screen recordings for public display, including visible profile, trip, and vehicle details. The clips document specific screens only; the written case study remains available independently of the recordings.

linkFallback: The public repository is available; no hosted demo is linked.
